name: application-typography
title: Typography
description: A type scale of real heading, paragraph, blockquote, list, and utility text elements for keeping text hierarchy consistent across a page or app.
useWhen: Establishing a consistent heading and body-text scale across a page or feature.
Rendering long-form content that needs real headings, a blockquote, a list, and inline code.
Replacing ad hoc font-size and font-weight utilities with a shared, named type scale.
avoidWhen: You only need a single label or metric value — use application-stat-tile or a plain span instead.
The eyebrow/metric/helper trio is what you need — use building-blocks-typography-primitives instead.
Rich text is user-authored — sanitize and render it separately rather than hardcoding structure.
responsiveBehavior: Text sizes are fixed per element; wrap the scale in your own responsive container to control max width and reduce heading sizes at narrow breakpoints if needed.
accessibility: Headings use real h1-h4 elements in descending order so the scale contributes a correct document outline.
Blockquote and list content use real blockquote and ul/li elements, not styled divs, so assistive tech announces them correctly.
Text and muted-text colors meet WCAG AA contrast against the surface they render on.

variants.title: Heading scale
variants.description: h1-h4 heading scale plus a lead paragraph, as typed string props rendered through real heading elements.
accessibility: Headings render in descending h1-h4 order so screen reader users can navigate the outline.

variants.title: Heading scale (Dark)
variants.description: Heading scale and lead paragraph adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Heading and lead text contrast must meet WCAG AA on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Body text
variants.description: Lead paragraph, running text, blockquote, list, and inline code as typed props rendered through real semantic elements.
accessibility: The quote renders as a real blockquote and the list as a real ul/li so assistive tech announces their semantics.

variants.title: Body text (Dark)
variants.description: Body-text elements adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Body text, blockquote, and inline code contrast must meet WCAG AA on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Utility sizes
variants.description: Large confirmation text, a form label, and muted helper text as typed props.
accessibility: The label renders as a real label element; pair it with a form control's id in your own usage.

variants.title: Utility sizes (Dark)
variants.description: Utility text sizes adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Muted text must still meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface, not just visually recede.
